claims.text: Robert Salas located his former missile commander Frederick Meiwald in the summer of 1996, and Meiwald wrote to him about the March 1967 incident on 1 October 1996. Robert Hastings additionally states that he tape-recorded a telephone conversation with Meiwald in August 1996 and spoke with him again on 6 May 2011.

THE CONTENTS OF THE 1 OCTOBER 1996 LETTER ARE DISPUTED AND THE BOARD HAS NOT READ IT. Salas and Hastings present it as elaborating and supporting the Oscar Flight account. Sceptical sources quote it as recording that Meiwald's recollection differs from Salas's and that he regrets being unable to help Salas establish his claims. Both characterisations are recorded; neither is adopted.

claims.source: Kevin Randle, 'Robert Salas and Me', 19 May 2013, http://kevinrandle.blogspot.com/2013/05/robert-salas-and-me.html , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: Kevin Randle records a discrepancy of substance between the two men rather than a disagreement about whether anything happened: Salas placing all ten missiles off alert and Meiwald four or five. Randle nonetheless assesses Meiwald as having confirmed what Salas said.

label: Col. Frederick Meiwald
narrative: Frederick Meiwald is the single most important corroborating name in the Oscar Flight claim and the board cannot presently say what he corroborated. He was Robert Salas's crew commander in the Oscar Flight capsule at Malmstrom, and after Salas located him in the summer of 1996 he wrote to Salas on 1 October 1996 about the incident. That letter is the hinge of the case and it was not opened by the pass of 19 September 2026. Two flatly incompatible characterisations of it are in public circulation: Salas and Robert Hastings present it as elaborating and supporting the Oscar Flight account, and it is the item the board's own robert-salas node currently calls his most important corroboration; sceptical sources quote it as saying that Meiwald's recollection differs from Salas's and that he regrets being unable to help Salas establish his claims. Kevin Randle, who is neither, records a discrepancy of substance rather than of tone, with Salas saying all ten missiles went down and Meiwald four or five. The honest position is that the letter is a real dated artefact, that it is the thing that would settle a great deal, and that nobody working on this board has read it. Everything else attributed to Meiwald is audio held by an interested party: a tape-recorded telephone conversation in August 1996 and a further call on 6 May 2011, both Hastings's.
